concerns.concern: The paper never shows that the composite gives a net power-factor gain over a conventional bilayer. A rough benchmark using the authors' own Table S1 suggests a Pt/YIG bilayer matches or beats the best composite, because the composites' spin Seebeck coefficient is about ten times lower. A reference bilayer measured in the same setup is needed.
concerns.quote: The manuscript must show, ideally with a reference bilayer measured in the same setup, that trans-scaling yields a net gain.

concerns.concern: Effective conductivity alone is not a figure of merit, since it can be raised in thin-film devices simply by thickening the Pt. Table S1 omits the spin Seebeck coefficient and power factor of the reference devices, so the '2–3 orders of magnitude' claim says nothing about energy-harvesting capability.
concerns.quote: Table S1 lists σeff for reference devices but omits their S_SSE and PF.

concerns.concern: There is no control composite made from Pt-coated nonmagnetic garnet powder (GGG or YAG). Such a control would rule out Pt-only, geometric or thermal artifacts.
concerns.quote: No Pt-coated nonmagnetic garnet composite (GGG/YAG powder): this would rule out Pt-only or geometric/thermal artifacts.

concerns.concern: There are no coating controls to confirm the inverse spin Hall origin. A low spin-orbit coating (Cu, Al) should make the signal vanish, and a negative spin Hall angle coating (W, Ta) should reverse its sign.
concerns.quote: No negative-θSH coating (W, Ta): the signal should reverse sign. This is the classic ISHE fingerprint.

concerns.concern: The observed decrease in saturation magnetization does not exclude a trace metallic ferromagnet. A percolating Pt–Fe or Fe phase well below 1 vol% with a large anomalous Nernst effect could produce ~10 nV/K without measurably changing Ms.
concerns.quote: "Ms decreases, hence no FMM" is therefore not a bound.

concerns.concern: XRD is not sensitive enough to exclude minority phases. It would miss an interfacial Pt–Fe alloy, and the text admits α-Fe2O3/YFeO3 could not be distinguished. More sensitive probes are needed for a quantitative bound, such as Mössbauer, STEM-EELS/EDS across interfaces, and low-T M(H)/ZFC–FC.
concerns.quote: XRD sensitivity (~1–5 wt%, with broad, low-crystallinity Pt peaks) is similarly insufficient.

concerns.concern: No effective-medium or circuit model links the interfacial spin Seebeck effect to the composite coefficient, so the claim that the whole volume contributes is only pictorial. No grain-size series tests the length-scale argument (grain size versus magnon diffusion length).
concerns.quote: Without such a model, the claim that "the volume contributes" (Fig. 1d) is pictorial only.

concerns.concern: The Pt-thickness dependence is suspiciously weak. Doubling the Pt thickness from 15 to 30 nm (both much larger than the spin diffusion length) should roughly halve the ISHE field, yet the coefficient drops only 15–20%. This may point to incomplete coverage, a different shunting geometry or extra contributions.
concerns.quote: Calling this "qualitatively consistent with the typical Pt thickness dependence" is not justified.

concerns.concern: The Pt shells are not characterized in the actual sintered 15/30 nm composites; TEM exists only for the 5 nm and 2.5 nm as-coated powders. The claimed continuity of the Pt network after 350–500 MPa compaction is therefore unverified.
concerns.quote: The claim of "continuous Pt channels" after 350–500 MPa compaction (which can crack, smear or delaminate shells) is therefore unverified.

concerns.concern: The measured effective conductivity is 1–2 orders below what a connected Pt network with this Pt content would give. This points to cracked shells, poor connectivity or contact resistance, which limits the power factor but is not analyzed.
concerns.quote: The measured 5×10²–5×10³ S/m points to poor shell connectivity, cracked shells or high contact resistance from pressing.

concerns.concern: The magnetization axis (±0.04 emu/g) is inconsistent with YIG's Ms of about 27 emu/g at 300 K. The quoted 37.9 emu/g looks like a low-temperature value, suggesting a ~10³ unit or normalization error.
concerns.quote: This apparent ~10³ unit or normalization error must be resolved.

concerns.concern: The composites' Ms is reduced by 20–25% regardless of Pt thickness, which simple mass dilution by Pt cannot explain. This hints at a magnetically degraded YIG surface or normalization errors, both relevant to the interfacial effect.
concerns.quote: A reduction that is large and t-independent hints at:

concerns.concern: A linear Hall signal shows only that the ordinary Hall effect of the Pt network dominates. It cannot bound a minority ferromagnetic phase whose thermal (anomalous Nernst) contribution could exceed its electrical (anomalous Hall) visibility.
concerns.quote: It cannot bound a minority ferromagnetic phase whose ANE (thermal) contribution could exceed its AHE (electrical) visibility.

concerns.concern: There is no field-angle rotation scan, including field parallel to the temperature gradient, to verify that the field scales with ∇T×M.
concerns.quote: No H∥∇T measurement or field-angle rotation scan verifying E ∝ ∇T×M.

concerns.concern: The temperature dependence of the signal is not measured for comparison with known YIG/Pt behaviour. Its sign is not compared with a reference YIG/Pt bilayer.
concerns.quote: No temperature dependence (e.g., the characteristic YIG SSE T-dependence) and no comparison of sign with a reference YIG/Pt bilayer.

concerns.concern: The field dependence of the signal is not overlaid on M(H) measured on the same piece in the same orientation. The signal saturates at higher fields than M(H) and differs in shape between configurations. Sample dimensions are missing, so demagnetization cannot be assessed.
concerns.quote: Overlaying Ey(H)/Ey^sat with M(H)/Ms, measured on the same piece in the same orientation, is needed

concerns.concern: Room-temperature-pressed samples give about twice the coefficient of 300 °C samples, which is not explained. Possible causes such as oxidation or interdiffusion in air, Pt recrystallization, changed spin-mixing conductance or porosity are not investigated; pressing in vacuum or inert gas could be considered.
concerns.quote: Possible causes, none of which is investigated:

concerns.concern: The isotropy claim rests on one sample measured in two configurations with different thermal contact setups (sapphire with grease versus Cu with tape). Their temperature-gradient errors differ and are unquantified, so the close agreement may be fortuitous.
concerns.quote: the 14.4 vs 14.8 nV/K agreement may be partly fortuitous.

concerns.concern: Isotropy is expected anyway from orientation averaging in a random composite, so it does not discriminate between mechanisms.
concerns.quote: It is therefore not a strong discriminator of mechanism.

concerns.concern: Uniaxial pressing could make the Pt connectivity anisotropic. The pressing axis is not specified relative to x, y, z, and conductivity and thermal conductivity are not reported along both directions.
concerns.quote: The relation of x, y, z to the pressing axis is not given, and σ and κ are not reported along both directions.

concerns.concern: The temperature-gradient metrology is under-specified. The gradient is taken from the total ΔT including interfaces with an unquantified error, and two different contact schemes are used. Sample dimensions and electrode geometry are not reported; heat-flux normalization or on-sample sensing is needed.
concerns.quote: The error is argued to be smaller for low-κ samples but is never quantified.

concerns.concern: Reproducibility is weak. All samples come from a single batch with one specimen per condition, there are no uncertainties on the coefficient or power factor, and error bars grow at high gradients.
concerns.quote: All samples come from "a single batch", with one specimen per condition.

concerns.concern: Absolute performance (power factor ~10⁻¹³ W/mK²) is many orders below bulk anomalous Nernst and Seebeck materials, and no output power, load matching or thermopile is shown. Yet the abstract and conclusion claim a scalable platform, so the language should be tempered.
concerns.quote: The language "bridging nanoscale spin caloritronics with macroscopic device integration" should be tempered or supported.

concerns.concern: The novelty is incremental-to-moderate, since bulk SSE/ANE composites were already reported (e.g., Boona et al. 2016). The headline scalability claim lacks a demonstrated performance advantage.
concerns.quote: The conceptual step is therefore incremental-to-moderate.

concerns.concern: The 15 and 30 nm Pt thicknesses are inferred from deposition time assuming a linear rate, not measured (e.g., by TEM, ICP-MS or XRF).
concerns.quote: The 15 and 30 nm thicknesses are inferred from deposition time assuming a linear rate. They are not measured

concerns.concern: The grain-size distribution of the crushed crystals is not quantified, although it controls Pt volume fraction, interface area and the magnon-length argument.
concerns.quote: The grain size distribution of the crushed crystals is not quantified

concerns.concern: Relative density is computed against YIG density alone, ignoring the much denser Pt, so the true relative density is lower than the reported 67–75%.
concerns.quote: The true relative density is therefore lower than 67–75%.

concerns.concern: Attributing the low thermal conductivity to phonon scattering at YIG/Pt interfaces is speculative. Porosity and inter-grain contact resistance could explain it, and no modelling is given.
concerns.quote: Attributing the reduction to "enhanced phonon scattering at the YIG/Pt interface" is speculative without such modelling.

concerns.concern: Using laser-flash diffusivity on porous, metal-networked samples needs justification, such as transparency or coating and radiation corrections.
concerns.quote: Laser-flash diffusivity on porous, metal-networked samples also needs justification

concerns.concern: Passing 100 mA through a porous, partially percolating Pt network during the Hall measurement could cause Joule heating and thermal artifacts, which are not addressed.
concerns.quote: Possible thermal artifacts in this measurement are not addressed.

concerns.concern: The known small nonlinear AHE-like signal in Pt/YIG, related to spin Hall magnetoresistance, is not discussed.
concerns.quote: The known small, nonlinear AHE-like signal in Pt/YIG (SMR-related) is not discussed.

concerns.concern: The text says the rotated configuration agrees with the H_x–∇zT configuration when it should say H_z–∇xT.
concerns.quote: A typo states that the rotated configuration agrees with "the H_x–∇zT configuration"; it should read H_z–∇xT.

concerns.concern: FePt and Y2O3 are given the same PDF reference number.
concerns.quote: FePt and Y₂O₃ share the same PDF number (#43-0661).

concerns.concern: The Cu-Kα wavelength is stated inconsistently between Methods and Note S2.
concerns.quote: The Cu-Kα wavelength is given as 0.15406 nm (Methods) vs 0.15418 nm (Note S2).

concerns.concern: Note S2 refers to Fig. S2 when it means Fig. S3.
concerns.quote: Note S2 refers to "Fig. S2" when it means Fig. S3.

concerns.concern: The '630% higher' power-factor comparison is ambiguous, since the ratio is about 7.3×.
concerns.quote: The "630% higher" PF comparison is ambiguous (5.1/0.7 ≈ 7.3×).

concerns.concern: The Author Contributions mention VSM while Methods describes SQUID magnetometry.
concerns.quote: the Author Contributions statement mentions VSM while Methods describes SQUID

concerns.concern: There are minor textual errors: the author name order 'Hirata Keisuke' and the phrase 'worth nothing'.
concerns.quote: the author name order "Hirata Keisuke"; "worth nothing".
